subject.title: fix: stabilize embedded prompt caching across policy and Responses boundaries

question: Should OpenClaw intentionally keep protected `computer`, `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes` schemas model-visible to denied turns, relying on immutable turn grants and pre-execution denial for authority?
rationale: This is an intentional security and product boundary change. Source inspection can verify the proposed gates, but only maintainers can accept schema visibility as the permanent contract across embedded and CLI/MCP runtimes.

options.title: Accept visible schemas with hard gates
options.body: Keep the cache-stable catalogue, require exact-head allowed and denied proof, and preserve focused invariant tests across all execution families.

options.title: Preserve hidden denied schemas
options.body: Reject this boundary and redesign cache stability so denied turns never receive protected schemas.

recommendation.title: Accept visible schemas with hard gates
recommendation.body: Keep the cache-stable catalogue, require exact-head allowed and denied proof, and preserve focused invariant tests across all execution families.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work owns the overlapping Gateway, CLI bundled-MCP grant, provenance, revocation, and embedded stream-selection authority paths.
